controller_guard.counts: host ^Action: <name> markers, in frozen order, stops at the first missing or out-of-order tool
cannot_be_fooled_by: prose claiming the remaining tools were already called
repeating a tool that was already called
any text the model writes, because the guard reads only host markers
controller_guard.only_added_text: one control message, on the rejection path only
controller_guard.view_assertion: byte-identical view (SHA256 of the served message view) versus the frozen r13 mechanism for the same prepared messages; GUARD_PREFIX never appears in a served view

void_bound.why: booked only once-only first-frame text; the whole frame is re-sent every call.  Measured same-work saving +35.16% = 3.43x the old bound

manifest.citable_note: both flags stay false until the independent audit passes all three acceptance conditions; the audit decides, not this file
manifest.failure_policy: preserve sample failure and continue unless provider unavailable or request cap

acceptance.unit_count: per-arm units = 4 tasks x 3 repeats = 12 (NOT r13's 16)
acceptance.condition_1_behaviour: plugin tool_sequence_consistent = 12/12 and per-task not below baseline; first_pass_facts not below baseline; guard_exhausted = 0
acceptance.condition_2_quality: strict and semantic success not below baseline per task and overall
acceptance.condition_3_cost: same work (equal agent call counts and first-role traces) and the corrected call-wise bound positive on the majority and in the batch mean; fewer tool calls or fewer model calls never count as saving
acceptance.verdict_rule: all three required for a valid saving candidate; otherwise 'not_passed_quality_gate'

guard_failure_semantics.exhausted: a role that never emits HANDOFF after guard_max_rejections push-backs is recorded with guard_exhausted = true and booked as a FAILED unit; it is excluded from every saving claim and the audit refuses to let it count as a success
guard_failure_semantics.extra_requests: every rejection re-send is a real agent request and is charged to the arm and to the global ledger
guard_failure_semantics.cap: the global request cap is a hard wall; reaching it stops the batch and continuation uses a new id plus --resume, never a partial grid

stop_line: guard exhausted in more than 30 percent of plugin units
homogeneity_boundary: the four tasks share the constructed 14-pair filler history (31 messages, 2,344-2,377 characters at repeat 0), so a narrow per-task band is an artefact of one design round; cross-task uniformity is NOT evidence of task-level heterogeneity, and per-task means plus dispersion must be reported with this caveat
tasks_are_no_longer_blind: these four tasks were constructed while the guard was designed, so the guard is not blind to them; this batch can only answer whether the guard makes the role finish the frozen tool table in this shape, not whether it generalises
missing_before_payment: no r16 payload acquisition exists, so no r16 bound is measured; the r16 projection in .tooling/bound_crewai_callwise_v16.py is a projection only and must not admit a paid batch
the guard has run end to end only in --mode mock, where it was never triggered (the mock model always completes the 4 tools); real triggering is unobserved
the 280 request cap assumes zero rejections; a non-zero rejection rate needs the stop-and-resume plan to be declared as planned behaviour
self_hash_of: the freeze content with every freeze_sha256 value left empty; a file cannot contain its own digest, so the batch manifest records this value and the auditor recomputes it
revision_discipline: immutable once written; any revision requires a *_FREEZE_AMENDMENT_<date>.json recording what changed, why, and the old and new SHA256

unpinned_on_purpose.why: the zero-API gate verifies this freeze, so pinning the gate would invalidate the freeze whenever the gate is extended; the gate's green result is a recorded precondition instead
